text:
jessica: hey team — running into a funky streaming issue with the python SDK. generator returned by `client.stream()` just stops yielding and never finishes when the model emits emoji. suspected it's when a multibyte emoji gets split across SSE chunks and we also had an auth rotation around the same time. any ideas? :confused:

mike: thanks for the report. can you paste minimal repro + SDK version + python version?

jessica: sure. python 3.10.11, redwood-python 0.8.2. minimal repro (sync-ish):
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
iter = client.stream("generate", {"prompt": "emoji test"})
for token in iter:
    print(token, end='')
# in our case the loop prints some tokens then just hangs forever, no exception
```

mike: any raw HTTP/SSE fragments or logs? also did you have token refresh happening (rotating creds) around the hang time?

jessica: yes — we rotate app-level keys every 5m using an internal pull. attached raw fragment capture from tcpdump (reconstructed, trimmed):
```
event: message
data: {"delta":"Hello \uD83D"}

# next chunk a few ms later:
event: message
data: {"delta":"\uDE0A"}

# then keepalive heartbeat:
event: keepalive
data: 

# then auth refresh header exchange (we see 401 -> 200 retry)
```
The first chunk ends with a half of the surrogate pair. python's utf-8 decode on the chunk boundary throws off the incremental parsing and generator doesn't yield or resume. also saw `401` at the same window because our proxy fetched a new token.

sara: interesting. two possible causes: 1) SSE framing/parsing mishandles partial multibyte sequences and blocks trying to decode, 2) retry/auth-rotate path doesn't re-drain the parser correctly so generator waits on buffered state.

mike: can you share the exact SDK call config? are you using `streaming=True` default decoder, or passing `text_mode` etc?

jessica: default `stream()` call, no custom params. this happens reliably when the model outputs emoji in the middle of a sentence. tried forcing `utf-8` explicitly locally but it still stalls.

support-bot: automated note — we've escalated this to eng-runtime with severity low->medium. Ticket #IR-1122 created.

mike: quick workaround while we dig: 1) pin an SDK version we know has an alternative streaming path (try 0.9.0-beta which contains an incremental decoder change), or 2) use a small shim to reassemble bytes using codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8') before feeding to SDK parser. Example shim (quick):
```py
import codecs
decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
# when you get a bytes chunk from SSE transport:
text = decoder.decode(chunk_bytes, final=False)
# append text to parser buffer
```
That handles split multibyte sequences safely.

jessica: thx — will try. any chance this is related to the auth rotation? when the 401/refresh happened the client retried and we saw the generator hang only after the refresh.

sara: possible. if the retry layer reinitializes the HTTP connection but the SSE parser instance stays tied to the old socket buffer, you can get stuck waiting for completion that never comes. need to confirm in v0.8.2 code paths. mike, can you reproduce by forcing a token refresh mid-stream?

mike: I'll try a repro: start a small toy server that emits a surrogate-split emoji across two separate chunked SSE messages, and in the middle simulate a 401 + token swap then resume stream. planning to run locally and attach logs.

eng-infra-bot: note: rotating creds observed at 2056001260 for jessica's workspace (automated rotation window).

mike: quick update — reproduced locally. using aiohttp server that yields: chunk1 b'data: {"delta":"Test \xF0\x9F'
chunk2 b'\x98\x8A"}\n
The incremental decoder matters — naive `chunk.decode('utf-8')` raises UnicodeDecodeError on chunk1 and our SSE parser swallowed that exception inside a coroutine producing no tokens and never finishing. also the retry flow on 401 reconnected but reused the same generator object which expected more bytes, so it blocked.

jessica: so combination of (a) naive decode per-chunk and (b) reconnection reusing parser instance. makes sense. what's the remediation plan?

mike: short term: update to 0.9.0-beta which uses incremental decoder and resets parser on reconnect. I'll post the PR link. medium term: add a unit test for surrogate-split sequences and a chaos test that forces auth rotation mid-stream. also add a better log when a UnicodeDecodeError occurs during streaming so it surface instead of silently swallowing.

sara: agree. I'll add an integration test to eng-runtime that simulates token rotation during streaming and check parser state reset. also we'll add a patch to ensure reconnect creates a fresh parser instance.

jessica: trying the shim now — the incremental decoder workaround avoided the hang locally. thanks.

mike: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rdw-python/pull/4512 — includes fix + tests. please try the wheel when CI finishes.

support-bot: update — linked PR queued for canary deployment. will notify after canary passes.

jessica: confirmed canary with 0.9.0-beta fixes it for our app. removing workaround. thanks all :pray:

mike: marking this resolved in thread; follow-ups: add observability metric for streaming decode errors and add docs note about rotating creds mid-stream.

sara: filed ENG-STREAM-43 to add chaos test.

jessica: closing on our side. leaving thread for records. :white_check_mark:
